title: Unbearably dull but not out of date
trail: In today’s Fiver: the perils of transfer deadline day, Keylor Navas and Stan Kroenke begs for spare change
body: TIME OF PUBCATION Transfer deadline day is always a difficult time for The Fiver, especially since Sky Sports News started shielding its reporters from purple joysticks. Now the only fun we can have is making up stories to arouse fans’ hopes but the social media contagion has made that an ultra-competitive field and, besides, there’s a genuine risk that by the time this arrives in your inbox, one of our fabrications could turn out to be true, so the joke would be on us. We could go the other route and announce that a certain club – say Manchester United or Tottenham – are not going to make any signings but the risk remains the same. We’re especially reluctant to claim that United can’t attract anyone because that’s precisely what José Mourinho suggested at his press conference early on Thursday, which makes The Fiver think he’s got something up his sleeve. Then again, that may just be a handkerchief to wipe more tears as Ed Woodward pursues targets in the manner of Weird Uncle Fiver chasing pigeons around a park after 10 too many tins. It may or may not be true that Woodward failed in a desperate late lunge at Diego Godín and that Spurs have snorted at his offer for Toby Alderweireld, but it is definitely the case that United’s interest in Harry Maguire reached a humiliating end, with noted funnyman Claude Puel getting laughs at the once-proud club’s expense. “I can confirm that [Maguire] is going to Manchester … but only for a couple of hours on Friday night with us,” announced the French comedian before Leicester’s match at Old Trafford on the opening day of the Premier League season. Perhaps United’s appeal, and perceptions that Puel is unbearably dull, are both out of date, but that’s not something that could be said about today’s Fiver, at least not at the time of going to pub. LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE NOW! Get some actual transfer news with our deadline day live blog. QUOTE OF THE DAY “I say this with force, I have the same desire to leave that I have to die” – Real Madrid goalkeeper Keylor Navas makes his feelings quite clear after Thibaut Courtois’ £35m arrival. SUPPORT THE GUARDIAN Producing the Guardian’s thoughtful, in-depth journalism [the stuff not normally found in this email, obviously – Fiver Ed] is expensive, but supporting us isn’t. If you value our journalism, please support us. In return we can hopefully arm you with the kind of knowledge that makes you sound slightly less uninformed during those hot reactive gegenpress chats you so enjoy. And if you think what we do is enjoyable [again, etc and so on – Fiver Ed], please help us keep coming back here to give you more of the same. FOOTBALL WEEKLY EXTRAAAAAAAA! Max Rushden is joined by Barry Glendenning, Andy Brassell and John Brewin for a bumper preview of the Premier League season. FIVER LETTERS “Did you realise that Adama Traoré could have caught the 10.55am ‘Do One’ from Middlesbrough to Wolverhampton (yesterday’s Bits and Bobs)? Not direct though, he would have had to change at Manchester Piccadilly and Crewe (arrives 2.57pm). Or he could have made only one change but he wouldn’t have got to Wolvo until 3.13pm” – David Morgans. “From a position of ignorance (nothing new here) my assumption is that football clubs treat buying players much like other businesses treat buying assets. They probably don’t use their own money but borrow instead, spreading the purchasing cost over a number of years (so it’s not €50m once off but €10m a year x 5 years). Much like buying a car on HP, there’s probably a residual value factored into the deal making it less expensive than it appears. If I’m correct – and look away now Jim White – we are completely misunderstanding the business of transfers. The fee is paid on the never-never, so it’s probably far less important than the players’ wages, which the club has to pay in real cash money every week or month. This could go some way to explaining José’s miserableness as he tries to distract attention from an obscene wages bill” – Adam Uncamus. “Yesterday, being daft enough to Still Want More, I followed your link to Rob Davies’s article on Stan Kroenke’s takeover of Arsenal. It portrayed the said Mr Kroenke but somewhat surprisingly he was wrapped in a grubby mac and holding a plastic cup labelled GIVE. Perhaps Arsenal cost a bit more than he expected?” – Tony Thulborn. “So The Fiver wants readers to believe its stereotypical cousin has ‘Sun Sea Sand’ in its name – should have pulled the other Juan” – Gareth Deeble. Send your letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. And if you’ve nothing better to do you can also tweet The Fiver. Today’s winner of our prizeless letter o’the day is … Tony Thulborn. BITS AND BOBS Mauricio Pochettino has been frantically scrambling around trying to find the positives in Tottenham’s transfer inactivity. “I think the club made a massive effort to try to extend contracts with people like Harry Kane. The club is doing an amazing effort to try to finish the stadium as soon as possible and the lodge is finished at the training ground,” he shrilled. José Mourinho may be miffed at Ed Woodward for not being given more money to waste, but that didn’t stop him from delivering a sideswipe at the media on Thursday morning. “It is difficult for me to believe we finished second [last season] because when I listen, when I read – not much but sometimes I do – you are capable of making people that finish second look like they were relegated, and people who win nothing, finish below us, you make them look like serial winners,” he humphed. Kepa Arrizabalaga has celebrated his move to Chelsea with a press conference, at which he answered several probing questions. He is happy to be at the club, thinks he can adapt to the manager’s style and likes that style too. Also, he is very fond of small animals and jigsaw puzzles. Elsewhere, Yerry Mina has had his medical at Everton, Leander Dendoncker has completed his move to Wolves, Leicester have snared Filip Benkovic from Dinamo Zagreb, West Ham have brought Lucas Pérez across town from Arsenal and Newcastle appear to have reached agreement with Swansea over the signing of Federico Fernández. And Roy Keane will captain a Manchester United team including Ryan Giggs, Rio Ferdinand, Paul Scholes and Gary Neville in a tribute match for Liam Miller in Cork next month. STILL WANT MORE? Daniel Sturridge, Jack Wilshere and Ross Barkley sounds like an interesting night out but for some reason Paul Doyle has written about how they – and others – have something to prove this season. Chelsea have paid £71.6m for a goalkeeper with one international cap, no senior medals and no experience of challenging for trophies. Ed Aarons explains why. Who doesn’t enjoy people making fools of themselves? Behold Michael Knighton, Grimsby Town and Classic YouTube. Usain Bolt is fast at running and also exceedingly famous. Can you guess which one of these skills has earned him a trial at Central Coast Mariners? It has been a summer of austerity in Turkish football. Emre Sarigul explains why this is good for young players. And roll up, roll up for the latest Premier League previews! No 17: Tottenham Hotspur and No 18: Watford. Oh, and if it’s your thing … you can follow Big Website on Big Social FaceSpace. And INSTACHAT, TOO! COLDER THAN A BLOCK OF ICE
